title: Meta app access token generated by the client_credentials call
summary: The app access token that the server-side client_credentials call returns, as distinct from the app-ID-and-secret pair passed in access_token.
rationale: Claim generation-call records the call and that it returns an app access token to use in place of a user access token; claim exposure-statements records that hard-coding the token exposes the app secret. The page shows no response body (open question generated-token-response-shape-unstated), so no member name or encoding is documented, token length is stated to vary (claim token-length-variable), and whether the token carries the standing of the app secret or can be rotated independently is not stated (generated-token-vs-secret-privilege). The pipe-joined pair is already covered by the existing app-secret pair Cases; which family owns the pair stays unsettled (composite-attribution-unsettled). Contract claims cited: app-access-token/generation-call, app-access-token/exposure-statements, app-access-token/token-length-variable.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for the generated token. Settled by: a Meta page that names the response member of the generation call and states the pair's classification.

sources.supports: Never hard-code app access tokens into client-side code or app binaries — doing so exposes your app secret and gives anyone who loads your webpage or decompiles your app full access to modify it.
sources.locator: App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

sources.supports: Therefore the App Secret or an App Access token should never be included in any code.
The length of access tokens changes over time as Meta updates what they store and how they are encoded.
